## Passages
RESULT [continual]: The choice of merge technique hardly matters: the knowledge accumulation of all techniques falls within one standard deviation across runs. Initialisation and deployment strategy are what matter. With ViT-B/16 CLIP on FoMo-in-Flux over 20 tasks: offline merging about 54.6%, offline+replay about 58.2%, plain replay about 59.1%.
US [continual]: For the professor's loop, a sensible deploy rule is to keep an EMA or merged 'accepted' model, train each increment from it, and deploy the merge, not the raw candidate. Rollback then means not folding the increment into the EMA. The paper also says not to spend a research cycle on fancy merge operators; plain replay is a hard baseline to beat.
CORRECTION [continual]: Confirmed: under Best-in-TIME (EMA init plus EMA deploy) the knowledge accumulation of all merge techniques lies within one standard deviation. ViT-B/16 on FoMo-in-Flux, 20 tasks: offline merging 54.6, offline+replay 58.2, replay 59.1.
